extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, corporate communicators, press-release writers and media-relations teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on composing, formatting, distributing, and measuring modern press releases for digital and global audiences, balancing legacy journalistic standards with new multimedia and measurement practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of a press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary purposes the press release still serves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the contemporary roles: SEO and search visibility; wire syndication for institutional credibility; newsroom archive of company news; scraping fodder for AI summarization tools; source material for analyst reports. Use releases not just to 'get coverage' but to support discoverability, credibility, archival needs and downstream data uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print-era format conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: How press releases were structured in the print era.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single format (text); distribution via fax and mail; 1-2 page maximum length; AP style strict adherence; single spokesperson quoted. These are historic constraints that influenced brevity, tone, and single-voice messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital-era format conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions that emerged with digital distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-format (text + multimedia); distribution via wire + email + social; length flexible (300–1,000 words); AP style preferred but not strict; multiple voices (executive + customer + partner). Embrace flexibility in length and sources of quote while retaining journalistic clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern format conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Current expectations for press-release packaging and assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a multimedia hub with downloadable assets; provide a social media kit with pre-formatted posts; pull out a tweet-length quote; offer translations for global reach; supply a mobile-optimized HTML version. Releases should be asset-rich and optimized for multiple channels and devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enduring journalistic standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Core journalism-driven elements that remain essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Need for newsworthy substance; 5 W's in the lede; AP style preference; named spokesperson contact; boilerplate at end; use of the '###' end marker. Despite format changes, a release must still read like news and answer basic reporting questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid distribution strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended mix of channels to maximize credibility and coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine wire services for institutional credibility and SEO, direct journalist outreach for actual coverage, social media for amplification, newsroom posting for owned media, and newsletter inclusion for engaged audiences. Choose channels thoughtfully based on goals (visibility vs. earned coverage vs. owned engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and evaluation evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: How success metrics have changed and should be tracked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Old metric: impressions. Now: pickup, sentiment, business outcomes. Future focus: attribution to revenue/conversion. Measurement should move beyond vanity metrics toward sentiment and demonstrable business impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core requirements for a modern press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum elements required for a credible, usable release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive news; named spokesperson; verifiable claims; multimedia; clear contact information; and thoughtful distribution. These items are non-negotiable to ensure a release can be acted on by journalists, analysts, and downstream tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style preference and voice choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of style and quoted voices in contemporary releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP style remains preferred but is not strictly enforced in digital-era releases; multiple voices (executive, customer, partner) are now common. Maintain clear, journalistic prose while allowing flexible voice inclusion to add credibility and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit PR Week quality checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: PR Week's boiled-down checklist of modern quality markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid distribution strategy; multimedia hub with assets; multiple voices in quotes; mobile-optimized format; translation if global; measurement beyond impressions. This summary synthesizes the article's practical, actionable checklist for evaluating a press release.
